newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thailand's rising LPG exports hurt other sellers.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's rising LPG exports hurt other sellers.

text.p: Thailand's plans to become a net exporter of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) are on target, but its timing spells trouble for other sellers in an oversupplied market, industry sources said on Tuesday.
The Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) exported close to 10,000 tonnes of LPG in July, up from average monthly exports of 6,500 tonnes between January and June.
PTT LPG exports last year were only between 2,000 and 3,000 tonnes each month, traders said. But a PTT source said the company would begin exporting 10,000 tonnes every month starting in August.
The cargoes will be exported from Thailand's port at Mab Ta Phut and Sri Racha, the PTT source told Reuters.
Thailand had projected becoming a net LPG exporter by the middle of this year after the start-up of two of its joint venture refineries with Shell and Caltex in January and in May respectively.
Thailand's 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) Star refinery is a joint venture between PTT and Caltex Petroleum Corp, itself a joint venture between Chevron and Texaco Inc.
PTT owns 64 percent of the 130,000 bpd refinery and Caltex Petroleum 36 percent.
PTT's other joint venture refinery with the Royal Dutch/Shell Group began operations in January.
The 145,000 bpd refinery, 66 percent owned by the Royal Dutch Shell group and the rest by PTT, began production three months ahead of schedule, industry sources said.
"We export our cargoes to China, India and Vietnam," the PTT source said. "Half of the export supplies will be from the Caltex Star Refinery."
But Thailand exports were not well-received by existing sellers in the LPG spot market.
"They are adding to an already oversupplied market," said a trader in Hong Kong.
"Prices into China were already on a downtrend as more sellers have placed floating storages around southern China," he added.
LPG spot prices in China have fallen to under $40 premium per tonne over the Saudi benchmark price, down from a premium of more than $60 in the same period last year, traders said.
Profits have been sliced because sellers are undercutting each other to get a bigger piece of the market share, they said.
But PTT exports were expected to rise further.
PTT's gas separation plant No.4 in southern Khnaom is expected to come onstream this month and will produce 500 tonnes of LPG per day.
Together with its plant No.3 in Maptaphut, also due to come onstream this month, PTT will be hard pressed to dispose of the additional supply of LPG.
PTT statistics show that Thailand's LPG supplies hitting 70,000 bpd next year but demand at only 60,000 bpd. The surplus will continue until the end of the year 2000, the firm said.
